items.title: GeoPT: MIT CSAIL and Tsinghua researchers give AI models a 'feel' for physics to simulate wider range of real-world scenarios
items.summary_en: MIT CSAIL researchers, with collaborators at Tsinghua University, introduced GeoPT, a pre-training approach that exposes physics-simulation AI models to 1.3 million synthetic dynamics samples of objects interacting in 3D. MIT News reports GeoPT reaches peak performance twice as fast as prior state-of-the-art simulators, needs up to 60% less labeled data, and can generate high-fidelity simulations with over 100 million mesh points in seconds, with potential applications in predicting vehicle aerodynamics, structural deformation, and fluid behavior.
items.notes: [preprint, not yet peer-reviewed] The underlying paper appears to be an arXiv preprint (indexed on alphaXiv as arXiv:2602.20399, 'GeoPT: Scaling Physics Simulation via Lifted Geometric Pre-Training'); no conference/journal acceptance was confirmed in available sources. items.title: ShiftLens: MIT CSAIL fabrication system lets 3D-printed objects change surface appearance without electronics
items.summary_en: A team at MIT CSAIL, led by associate professor Stefanie Mueller with collaborators including undergraduate Dingning Cao, a TU Munich graduate student, and a Northeastern postdoc, built ShiftLens, a design-and-fabrication system for objects whose surface appearance changes when a user presses, slides, or turns part of the object. It combines a layer of lenticular lenses with a patterned backplane, both printable in a single pass on a multimaterial 3D printer; demonstrated prototypes include a bottle cap that shows a warning icon when loose and a tic-tac-toe board that changes its display via a knob.

items.title: Daniela Rus, CSAIL Director, receives 2026 Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize
items.summary_en: MIT News reports that Daniela Rus, Director of CSAIL and the Panasonic Professor of Computer Science, received the 2026 High-Tech Prize of the Bavarian Minister-President, awarded jointly by the Bavarian State Government and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, for contributions to self-organizing robot collectives, soft robotics, autonomous mobility, and brain-inspired AI, including her work on liquid neural networks. She accepted the award on July 23 in Munich.
